-1.sentence: The general spent all night going over his outfit.
-1.meaning1: any cohesive unit such as a military company
-1.focus_meaning: any cohesive unit such as a military company
precontexts: The general sat at a small desk and tapped a pencil hard against a sheaf of papers. From the flap of the tent came the shuffling and murmurs of people finishing their duties.
He woke before dawn and moved quietly across the house.
He went over the schedule one more time. A small rumble of activity moved through the house. Maps and notes were spread across the table as he made a final plan.
endings: At first light he stepped into the street to see if everything held together.

He spread things out on the table and checked them one by one. A knock on the door made him pause, and he wrote a short note before sealing it. By morning he stepped outside and watched as everything came together.
At dawn he walked the area, adjusting small things and speaking to those nearest. Satisfied, he closed the flap and walked toward the road.
-1.example1: The small outfit was sent to secure the mountain pass.
-1.example2: She wore a new outfit with matching shoes and a hat.

1.sentence: The music was very loud at the party; Tom thought it was a blast.
precontexts: String lights and a bobbing crowd filled the backyard.

Tom carried a case of beer into the apartment. He hung his jacket on a hook and greeted a few neighbors who were already there. Someone had plugged in a big speaker and people were arranging cups and snacks.
Tom answered the door and carried a stack of CDs into the living room. Guests squeezed past each other and someone set a bowl of chips on the table.
endings: A couple of neighbors stood under the streetlight and whispered. Tom laughed at something on his phone and went back to the crowd.

A sharp crash from the kitchen made several people jump. Thin smoke curled up near the back steps and someone yelled for everyone to step outside. Tom went to the door to look, telling others he'd call for help if it looked serious.
Later Tom stepped outside and found the street full of people talking about what they had heard.
1.example1: The blast from the dynamite echoed through the canyon.
1.example2: A blast shook the house and made the windows rattle.

3.sentence: After much thought, they finally decided to enlist.
precontexts: They spent the morning filling out forms and polishing shoes. A recruiter had asked them to come prepared with references and paperwork. At the doorway they paused, trading a look and folding the brochure back into its stack.
They gathered around a kitchen table and spread out maps and contact lists.
They had been arguing about the future all week. Plans were scattered across the kitchen table and bills needed attention.
endings: A clerk glanced up and called them in to begin the paperwork.
They signed the paperwork and scheduled a meeting. Neighbors watched as boxes were loaded into a van outside. When they left at sunrise, each felt both nervous and oddly relieved.
They signed the papers and shook hands with the person across the table. At dawn they left, carrying only what they thought they'd need.
3.example1: He decided to enlist in the army.
3.example2: We decided to enlist a tutor to help our son with math.

5.sentence: The draft arrived when they least expected.
5.meaning2: a document ordering the payment of money; drawn by one person or bank on another
precontexts: They were sweeping the kitchen and bickering about weekend plans. A soft knock came at the door, and something was slid beneath it before anyone could answer.
They had been making lists and packing a small suitcase.

They had been saving every extra coin while talking about possible futures. One evening someone at the table reached for the mailbox key and brought in an envelope with an official seal. They unfolded the paper, scanned it quickly, and glanced at each other.
endings: They bent down to pick it up and moved closer to read every line. One shrugged into a coat while the other dialed a number, both already deciding how to respond.

One of them unfolded the paper, breathing hard, while the other checked the calendar again. They argued briefly about whether to go now, then agreed to call the office shown on the page. When the call connected, they sat on the stairs and listened until a plan formed.
After a long silence they made a plan to respond before the week was over.
5.example1: He was called up for the draft last year.
5.example2: She paid the supplier with a bank draft drawn on her account.

11.sentence: Its armor protects it from stabs and cuts.
11.meaning1: protective covering made of metal and used in combat
11.meaning2: tough more-or-less rigid protective covering of an animal or plant
11.focus_meaning: protective covering made of metal and used in combat
precontexts: I heard scraping on the porch and went outside to see. Something small and dark had been wedged between the boards and it didn't struggle when I touched it.
Something small and steady was crossing the path outside my gate.

A low silhouette moved along the fence line at dawn. It paused under the lamplight and tilted its head at the sound of footsteps. Someone in the yard tossed a scrap, and it darted forward to catch it.
endings: I crouched down to watch it move closer. When I touched its side, I felt only a faint vibration under my fingers. I left it alone and went back inside, trusting the shelter would be enough until morning.
By the time the sun rose it was gone, leaving only the scrap where it had stood.
I rinsed it under the tap and the water beaded on the surface. When the sun warmed it, something inside shifted and I carried it back to the yard.
11.example1: The knight's armor protected him in combat.
11.example2: The armadillo curled into a ball, its armor protecting it from predators.

13.meaning1: a soldier in a motorized army unit
13.focus_meaning: a soldier in a motorized army unit
precontexts: They had been following the dark pickup for ten miles when headlights flashed behind them.
They drove along the dusty road toward the bridge. A pickup pulled up and told them to stop for inspection. One of the men reached into his coat and moved toward the rear doors.
They had been following the black SUV along the interstate for miles. Inside the pursuing vehicle, someone checked a map and tapped the dash with nervous fingers.
endings: The man in the cab fell forward as the truck swerved onto the shoulder. A second vehicle pulled alongside and someone shouted into a handset. They put the wounded man into the rear and drove off toward the distant lights.
Shouts spilled from both cars as the SUV fishtailed and hit the curb. By the time backup arrived, witnesses were being directed to the shoulder and an evidence team began photographing the scene.
The others were forced out and the vehicle drove off, leaving one person on the ground.
13.example1: The trooper rode in the armored vehicle during the patrol.
13.example2: The trooper directed traffic after the highway accident.

17.meaning2: a person who keeps watch over something or someone
17.focus_meaning: a military unit serving to protect some place or person
precontexts: We packed the last boxes and checked the radio for departure instructions. A signal flashed at the gate and someone ran back to tell us to hold position.
The small compound smelled of diesel and wet earth as lights blinked along the fence.
We had packed our gear and checked the radios. Someone at the gate kept calling for a replacement. The generator failed during the night, so we tightened the schedule.
endings: We closed the hatch, double-checked the manifest, and kept an eye on the gate. A mechanic kneeled by the nearest panel, tapping at a corroded hinge to keep the bitter cold at bay. Finally, headlights appeared, the gate slid open, and we drove off into the gray morning.
An hour later a convoy rolled in and people stepped out carrying paperwork under the lights. Once they inspected the manifest we loaded the last crate and drove off.
We handed over the keys and drove off before dawn.
17.example1: A guard of soldiers stood outside the embassy to protect the ambassador.
17.example2: The guard watched the gate all night.

19.sentence: He was forced into an unconventional hold.
precontexts: They had found his hiding spot in the derelict mill.

They cornered him behind the warehouse and demanded the package. He ducked through a rusted door and stumbled down a narrow stair. At the bottom he tumbled into a dim chamber where two figures waited with a length of chain.
Footsteps echoed inside the building as people prepared to move. They guided him toward the only covered space they had found.
endings: He tried to steady himself, fearing a wrong move would spoil the rest of the effort. When the door clicked shut, someone pressed a folded note into his hand and stepped back.

A forearm dug into his side as someone muttered instructions he didn't understand. At the same time, others stacked crates against the shutters and bolted the entrance. He tried to make sense of it all while counting heartbeats instead of breaths.
They led him deeper inside and bolted a metal gate behind them.
19.example1: The castle was the last hold against the invading army.
19.example2: She tightened her hold on the rope.

21.meaning2: tending to become more severe or wider in scope

precontexts: A late-night radio message reported movement off the coast. Local volunteers grabbed binoculars and trained them toward the dark horizon. On the shore, a faint glow had been growing for several minutes.
Someone radioed that something had stirred out by the breakwater before dawn.
People along the bay had been watching the horizon since dawn. A low rumble came from out there, and tiny lights bobbed where sea met sky.
endings: Someone reached for the radio while others edged toward the water.
Boats near the pier cut their engines and neighbors climbed onto roofs to get a better look. Some whispered plans while others checked radios, unsure whether to warn the town or to celebrate.

A pair of small craft changed course and headed toward the light. On shore, officials spread maps and made notes while others moved gear to the quay. By midday they had roped off the nearest docks and told everyone to keep back.
21.example1: The navy kept two destroyers active in the region.
21.example2: The wildfire is active and likely to spread to nearby communities.

precontexts: Morning standup stretched as people took longer to get set up at their desks. A notice appeared asking staff to expect intermittent access to shared resources and delays in email delivery. The schedule showed more people out than expected and calls to the support line had doubled.
On Monday the office felt off and the usual energy was missing.
Phones lit up at the front desk and people lingered in the kitchen, talking quietly. Messages piled up about unexpected absences and unexplained file errors.
endings: By afternoon, meetings were rescheduled and leadership promised a quick plan to get things back on track.

113.example2: The virus replicated inside his cells and caused the infection.

119.sentence: The priest got up and stood infront of the crowd, taking the speech out of his pocket as he prepared to deliver.
precontexts: People filled the chairs in the hall and traded low words as the lights dimmed. A man in a dark jacket smoothed a folded note and glanced toward the front.

The small hall filled with people taking their seats and murmuring among themselves. An usher moved down the aisle passing around a stack of folded papers. Someone in the front row closed their eyes and reached for a hand held out beside them.
People shuffled their feet and glanced toward the front as the room grew expectant.
endings: He paused only a moment, looking at the papers, then began.
He slowed his breathing and several people in the front row closed their eyes. When he finished, the crowd left quietly, some stepping forward to touch the hem of his coat.

He cleared his throat and unfolded the paper, eyes moving over the first line. Some people bowed their heads while others straightened, waiting for what would come next. When he began, his voice was steady and low, and the room shifted to match the tone.
119.example1: Jesus came to deliver us from our sins.
119.example2: She will deliver the keynote speech at the conference tomorrow.

121.focus_meaning: render holy by means of religious rites

There was a knock at the door and I answered it.
I pushed a chair by the window and waited. A knock came sooner than I expected and I opened the door.
endings: Before he left he folded a small envelope and pressed it into my hand, then walked away without another word.
He folded his coat, took the cup steadily, and glanced at a small packet on the saucer. After he left I found a thin sprig tucked under the packet and a slip with a few careful words.

He put down a thermos and a tin of biscuits, then sat at my small kitchen table. He murmured a few quiet words and folded his hands before we drank. After he left I found a plain coin tucked into my teacup and felt oddly light as I shut the door.
121.example1: The priest will bless the church.
121.example2: May this new home bless your family with joy and prosperity.

145.sentence: Years of loss and failure had left her with unshakeable, temporal pain.
145.meaning1: of or relating to the temples (the sides of the skull behind the orbit)
145.focus_meaning: of or relating to the temples (the sides of the skull behind the orbit)
precontexts: She had been out of work for a year and learned to count every small expense. Her days shrank to routines and evenings she opened a battered box of old photos. Tonight she sat by the window with an ice pack pressed to her head while rain ran down the pane.

She opened the attic box and found a bundle of faded letters and a thin program from a small ceremony. She sat on the floor and smoothed the corners while the afternoon sun warmed the room and a low throbbing began near her ear.
She walked into the clinic carrying a small paper bag of pills and a folded list of names.
endings: She pressed the heel of her hand against the side of her head and whispered that she couldn't always bear to go through the old boxes again. Instead she carried a single photograph to the sink, held it under the tap until the water blurred the ink, and decided to throw the rest away.

When the nurse asked her to recount what had happened, she read dates and brief notes as if checking wounds. Back in her apartment she laid the list across the table beside a chipped cup and let the rain blur the page. Before sunrise she taped one more entry under the old lamp and told herself she would try a different path, even if the ache stayed.
She closed the box, put the ice pack back in the freezer, and decided to call someone in the morning.
145.example1: She felt a sharp pain in her temporal area on the side of her skull.
145.example2: Temporal comforts vanish, reminding us that nothing lasts forever.

When the session ended they booked another visit and packed the folder back into their bag. As they left they paused on the sidewalk and dialed a number, speaking in a steady voice.

297.example2: Her constant perfectionism was compensation for deep-seated feelings of inadequacy.

endings: The beam engaged and a thin line moved across the plate while voices rose behind me. Someone jotted numbers on a clipboard and another person replayed a clip on a phone. When the run finished I saved the logs and then listened as people argued about what it meant.
I ran the calibration and watched the numbers on the monitor inch forward. We packed the parts and waited for the client's confirmation by email.
We left it for the committee to decide and slid the panel back under the tarp.
384.example1: The deflection of the beam under the load was clearly visible.
384.example2: The judge's deflection of judgment led to several unfair sentences.

385.sentence: The effect radiates in that direction, outwards, across the hills.
385.meaning2: extend or spread outward from a center or focus or inward towards a center
precontexts: The crew set up the instruments on the ridge before dawn. A low hum had started underfoot and the monitor's needle flicked once.
They flip the switch on the small transmitter and wait.
A technician climbed the ridge and checked the old transmitter. Back in town people looked up and whispered when the sky brightened. A low hum ran across the valley, making cups tremble on porches.
endings: They agreed to cut power and walk to the site at dusk.
A distant band of trees shimmered and a dog began to whine down in the valley. They packed up quickly, unsure if they had recorded something useful or if it had been a trick of the landscape.

A flock of crows launches from the hedgerow and a dog on the far farm begins barking. Someone on the valley road waves their arms as a pale glow moves over the fields. As dusk falls they pack the gear into the car and drive back without an answer.
385.example1: The radio antenna will radiate signals across the city.
385.example2: Ripples radiate outward from the point where the stone hit the pond.

387.sentence: The scientists had finally uncovered how fusion worked.
387.meaning1: a nuclear reaction in which nuclei combine to form more massive nuclei with the simultaneous release of energy
387.meaning2: the state of being combined into one body
387.focus_meaning: a nuclear reaction in which nuclei combine to form more massive nuclei with the simultaneous release of energy
precontexts: A team had spent years running late-night trials under the hum of fluorescent lights. They adjusted dials, logged data, and argued over readings when a sudden spike appeared on the monitor. A technician cross-checked the instruments and wheeled a prototype device into the center of the room.
A rain-soaked van rolled up to the warehouse and a researcher climbed out carrying a battered notebook.
They locked the lab doors and checked the power feed one last time. They placed two separate pieces on the bench, their edges matched along a faint seam.
endings: The monitors jumped and a steady tone filled the room as readings climbed. Outside, the streetlights brightened and neighbors peered from windows at the steady glow.
They recorded the results, locked down the lab, and drafted a message for the oversight board.

They wheeled a covered crate into the center and unplugged a cord, hands moving quickly. A hospital phoned across town asking for an immediate explanation, so the team split to prepare a demonstration. By midnight the light above the lab window changed color, and everyone let out a breath they hadn't known they'd been holding.
387.example1: Fusion happens when atomic nuclei combine to form heavier nuclei and release energy.
387.example2: The fusion of the two companies created a single corporation.

389.sentence: The engineer knew the moment would determine whether the bridge held.
389.meaning1: a turning force produced by an object acting at a distance (or a measure of that force)
389.focus_meaning: a turning force produced by an object acting at a distance (or a measure of that force)
precontexts: Rain slicked the girders as he tightened the last bolt and checked the load gauge.

A crew had spent weeks assembling the span over the river. They tightened bolts and checked supports as a low fog rolled in. The engineer stepped onto the control platform and checked the instruments again.
Crews had sealed the joints and walked the length of the span. A police car idled at one end while a crane held a heavy cable near the center.
endings: He signaled the crew and the last clamp was released. The deck trembled, then settled as cars rolled across and the workers exhaled.

He eased the winch until the cable took the strain and the span settled a few inches. A foreman called that traffic would start in five minutes and the crew waited on his signal. When the span held, he unclipped his harness and waved the flag to let the first car through.
He watched the cables groan and the deck tilt a few degrees before the structure settled and the crew cheered.
389.example1: He used a longer wrench to increase the moment and loosen the bolt.
389.example2: At that moment, the lights went out.

391.sentence: The various strains left his body feeling heavy.
391.meaning1: (physics) deformation of a physical body under the action of applied forces
391.meaning2: difficulty that causes worry or emotional tension; ; - R.J.Samuelson
391.focus_meaning: (physics) deformation of a physical body under the action of applied forces
precontexts: He started before dawn, hauling cinderblocks from the truck to the foundation. Midday the landlord called about the inspection and the voice on the line was sharp. He tightened bolts on a sagging beam while his hand kept brushing at the fresh cuts on his palm.
He unloaded the last box from the truck. He had spent the morning answering calls and lifting heavy furniture.
He had spent the morning moving a stack of metal panels and returning call after call.
endings: He paused at the garage door and pressed his palms to his knees to steady himself. A dinged panel and a crumpled invoice lay at his feet, each bringing a different memory to the surface. He sat down on an upturned bucket and dialed the number he had been avoiding since dawn.
He sank onto the porch steps and rubbed his shoulders. His phone buzzed again, and he debated whether to stand up or leave the work until tomorrow.
After closing up his toolbox he sank onto the stoop and watched the sun track toward the roofline.
391.example1: The engineer measured the strain in the steel beam as the heavy truck crossed the bridge.
391.example2: The financial strain of paying the bills kept her up at night.

393.sentence: The masseuse felt the tension increase as he touched the thigh of his awkward patient.
393.meaning1: (physics) a stress that produces an elongation of an elastic physical body
393.meaning2: (psychology) a state of mental or emotional strain or suspense
393.focus_meaning: (physics) a stress that produces an elongation of an elastic physical body
precontexts: The masseuse unlocked the clinic, warmed the oil, and checked the appointment book. The patient had called after a minor fall at work and said his thigh had been bothering him. He kept adjusting his shorts and stared at the ceiling as the masseuse helped him onto the table and covered his legs.
The masseuse laid out fresh towels and warmed a bottle of oil.
He warmed the oil between his hands and arranged the towel on the table. The patient kept shifting and cleared his throat every few moments.
endings: He hesitated for a beat and adjusted his hand, mindful of the patient's stiff posture. A distant truck rolled by and the rumble made the table give a faint shudder. They both breathed through the moment and by the time the session ended the patient offered a brief, grateful smile.
After a moment the masseuse asked if that felt right, altered his hand placement, and the patient let out a long breath.
The patient flinched and glanced at an elastic exercise band coiled on the shelf. The masseuse paused, adjusted his grip, and asked whether he should ease off.
393.example1: The tension in the spring caused it to elongate.
393.example2: She felt tension building as the deadline approached.
